uncited: This family provides exact, closed-form solutions for the intersection of a ray with standard geometric primitives (spheres, planes, triangles, tetrahedra) by solving the underlying algebraic equations derived from their implicit or parametric definitions.

It differs from iterative methods like [Ray-Marching](52-ray-marching.md) or [Implicit Surface and SDF Intersection](2795-implicit-surface-and-sdf-intersection.md) by avoiding root-finding loops, and from [Ray-Volume and Bounding Box Intersection](10057-ray-volume-and-bounding-box-intersection.md) by handling specific primitive shapes rather than axis-aligned bounding volumes.
It serves as the foundational geometric primitive test for ray tracing and volume rendering pipelines.
Analytic ray-primitive intersection is a cornerstone of computer graphics, originating with the development of ray tracing algorithms in the early 1980s.
The geometric projection method for spheres and the Möller–Trumbore algorithm for triangles are standard implementations found in virtually all modern renderers.
These methods are used in offline rendering, real-time ray tracing, and scientific visualization involving unstructured grids.
